tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: WebFetch
tools.description:
Fetches a URL, converts the page to markdown, and answers `prompt` against it using a small fast model.

- Fails on authenticated/private URLs — use an authenticated MCP tool or `gh` for those instead.
- Fails on localhost and other hostnames without a dot; for a local server, use curl via Bash.
- HTTP is upgraded to HTTPS. Cross-host redirects are returned to you rather than followed; call again with the redirect URL.
- Responses are cached for 15 minutes per URL.

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

prompt.description: The prompt to run on the fetched content

offset.description: Character position in the page text to start reading from. Use it to read on through a page too long for one call, with the value the previous result gave.

tools.name: TaskStop
tools.description:
- Stops a running background task by its ID
- Takes a task_id parameter identifying the task to stop
- To stop an agent-team teammate, pass its agent ID or bare teammate name as task_id
- To stop a background agent spawned with a name, pass that name as task_id
- Returns a success or failure status
- Use this tool when you need to terminate a long-running task

task_id.description: The ID of the background task to stop. Agent-team teammates and named background agents are also accepted by agent ID or name.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

0	---
1	name: geeky-plan
2	description: Use when asked to turn a specification folder into a frozen implementation package. This skill creates implementation-plan.md, tasks, kanban, references, and handoff artifacts, runs planning gates, and outputs a package ready for `/geeky-implement`.
3	---
4	
5	Use the shared [workflow terminology](../../AGENTS.md#workflow-terminology).
6	
7	# geeky-plan
8	
9	Create a set of plan / tasks / Kanban based on provided research and specification requirements.
10	
11	This is the _planning_ phase. After this run, use the `plan-review` skill (or `/plan-review <folder>`) to audit the package, then the `geeky-implement` skill (or `/geeky-implement <folder>`) to execute it, or the `geeky-status` skill (or `/geeky-status <folder>`) to inspect state.
12	
13	## Input
14	
15	`<requirement>`: a user-provided specification, design file, research files, or a folder path specifying all of these. **IF MISSING, ask the user for it/them.** Throughout this document, references to `$ARGUMENTS` mean this requirement input.
16	
17	## Constitution
18	
19	**DO THIS SEQUENTIALLY IN THIS ORDER.** Resolve the working folder deterministically: if `$ARGUMENTS` is a folder path, use it; if it is one or more file paths, use the directory containing them; if it is a plain-text requirement with no files, ask the user for (or propose) a feature folder, e.g. `docs/<feature-name>/`, before creating any artifact. Save all artifacts in that folder.
20	
21	## Time budget and checkpoint
22	
23	At entry, before each numbered task or phase, after a lengthy direct operation,
24	and immediately before and after each worker dispatch or blocking wait, run
25	`python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/workflow-budget.py" --stage geeky-plan --json`.
26	Resolve `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` to the installed plugin root containing this skill
27	when the environment variable is unset, and use an available Python interpreter.
28	If the helper cannot run or its output is unreadable, stop and report the missing
29	budget check; do not assume unlimited time. Read the JSON status, not just the
30	exit code: `unbounded` means no deadline was provided; `active` continues; `reserve` or `exhausted` stops starting new work
31	and checkpoints the incomplete stage; `invalid` stops and reports the configuration
32	error. A zero exit also covers `reserve`, so it is not permission to continue.
33	The stage target is advisory, not a gate or guarantee: after it is exceeded,
34	finish required work with the smallest sufficient evidence and defer optional
35	expansion. Never skip a required review, validator or acceptance condition, or
36	claim an incomplete stage passed. Pass the hard deadline, closeout reserve, and
37	stage target from the check to every child brief. If the deadline is absent, say
38	unbounded; if only the target is absent, say the target is unavailable. Do not
39	invent either value. Tell each child to return its current evidence,
40	unresolved questions and status before the available work time ends. Bound waits by
41	the remaining usable time where the host supports it; if it cannot, record that
42	limitation rather than claiming cancellation. Recheck after a wait; a child report alone does not override the budget result.
43	
44	If the budget stops this stage, record missing artifacts, reviews and validators in the handoff; do not declare the package complete or frozen.
45	
46	## Tasks
47	
48	1. Build an implementation plan to satisfy all requirements in `$ARGUMENTS`.
49	
50	2. Save completed implementation plan to a markdown file `implementation-plan.md`.
51	
52	3. Deep-dive into the implementation plan and analyse it thoroughly to break it down into tasks.
53	
54	4. Create task markdown files using the canonical task template bundled with this plugin at `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/templates/task_template.md` (where `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is the root of the `geeky-orchestration` plugin). If for any reason that file cannot be read, fall back to the inline template below — but prefer the bundled one. A task must be clearly defined and self-contained. Each task includes tests to validate and verify the task BEFORE proceeding to the next task. Consider the order of the tasks, and name each task file with prefix `Tx-taskname` where `x` is the order number **starting at T1** (e.g., `T1-setup-database.md`, `T2-implement-auth.md`). Tests can be a separate file or within the task file itself.
55	
56	   If the bundled template is unreadable, use the inline fallback in
57	   `references/task-template-fallback.md` (kept in sync with `templates/task_template.md`;
58	   the bundled template is canonical).
59	
60	5. **Coverage check — MUST not miss anything.** Write `draft.md` to disk: a `# Coverage Matrix` table mapping every requirement in `$ARGUMENTS` to the task(s) that satisfy it. Required columns (exact): Requirement ID, Requirement Summary, Covered by Task(s), Status. Each requirement must have at least one task; each task must trace to at least one requirement. Then read `draft.md` back and verify completeness. Fix gaps before proceeding.
61	
62	6. Delegate a PM-style review of the plan + tasks as a whole. **Reviewer selection order (first match wins):**
63	   1. A `development-project-manager` agent if available in the environment
64	   2. A `planning-coordinator` agent if available
65	   3. A general-purpose subagent briefed with explicit PM-review instructions
66	   4. Perform the review directly in a dedicated pass
67	
68	   The review must check coverage, sequencing, dependency correctness, and scope gaps. Request actionable findings with requirement/task references and a concise verdict; avoid restating the package. Record suggestions separately from required fixes. Save the result as `review-development-project-manager.md` (exact filename — downstream skills look for it). Intelligently resolve all gaps but note them inside the review document.
69	
70	7. Create a Kanban markdown `kanban.md` for tracking task progress. Standard lanes: Backlog, Ready, In Progress, Blocked, In Review, Done, plus a Validation Checklist (release gate). Place every newly-created task in **Ready** unless an explicit dependency keeps it in Backlog.
71	
72	8. Create a markdown `references.md` containing references to the design docs, the plan, the task files, the tests, the kanban — with full descriptions and instructions for implementation. Double-check that nothing is missing.
73	
74	9. Create/Update `handoff.md` with a brief and detailed summary of this session's work, plus preparation and instructions for the next session. Explicitly recommend `plan-review <folder>` (the `plan-review` skill / `/plan-review` command) as the next step to audit the package, and `geeky-implement <folder>` after it passes.
75	
76	10. **Validation gate — run the deterministic checks before declaring the plan done.** Do not rely on judgment alone that the package is complete; run the bundled validators and fix until each exits 0 (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` is the plugin root; see `AGENTS.md` / `geeky.manifest.json` for the full invocation matrix):
77	    - Task-file schema: `python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-task-schema.py" --path "<folder>"`
78	    - Kanban integrity: `python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-kanban.py" --path "<folder>"`
79	    - Planning-folder completeness: `python "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-planning-folder.py" --path "<folder>"`
80	
81	    The `python` form works cross-platform; if Python is unavailable, use the paired PowerShell scripts, e.g. `pwsh -NoProfile -File "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/validate-task-schema.ps1" -Path "<folder>"` (same pattern for the other two).
82	
83	    If any exits non-zero, read its output, correct the artifact, and re-run until green. Only then finalize.
84	
85	## Acceptance criteria
86	
87	1. `implementation-plan.md`
88	2. `tasks/` folder with `Tx-taskname.md` files
89	3. PM review of plan + tasks (saved as `review-development-project-manager.md` — exact filename)
90	4. `kanban.md`
91	5. `references.md`
92	6. `handoff.md`
93	
94	Additional artifacts may be created beyond these.
95	
96	## Frozen planning contract
97	
98	These artifacts form the frozen contract between planning and implementation: after this skill completes, `implementation-plan.md`, `references.md`, and `tasks/Tx-*.md` (plus `feature-specification.md` and `draft.md` if present) are guarded against edits by the bundled PreToolUse hook. Downstream sessions record per-task notes in `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md` instead; `kanban.md` and `handoff.md` stay mutable. During this planning session, guard warnings on these files are expected while iterating to green.

0	# linkvault: Interface Contract
1	
2	## Constraints
3	
4	- **Stack:** Python >=3.11, stdlib only (`http.server`, `sqlite3`, `json`, `argparse`, `urllib`, `secrets`, `hashlib`, `threading`, `signal`); pytest for tests only.
5	- **Package location:** `linkvault/` at the workspace root (`linkvault/__init__.py`, `linkvault/__main__.py`); commands run with the workspace root as cwd.
6	- **Entry points:** `python -m linkvault serve ...` (server); `python -m linkvault <client-cmd> ...` (client).
7	
8	## Functional requirements
9	
10	- **R1 Server start.** `serve` opens or creates the DB, binds 127.0.0.1, then prints exactly one ready line to stdout. Nothing else is ever written to stdout; logs go to stderr.
11	- **R2 Token issuance.** `POST /v1/tokens` with the correct admin key returns a new token. The token is `lv_` followed by 32 lowercase hex characters (`secrets.token_hex(16)`). Only its SHA-256 hex digest is stored.
12	- **R3 Authentication.** Every `/v1/links` route requires `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. A missing, malformed or unknown token returns 401.
13	- **R4 Create link.** `POST /v1/links` stores `url` with a custom `slug` or a generated slug, and an optional `expires_in`.
14	- **R5 Slug rules.** Slugs are case-sensitive. A custom slug must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` and must not be `healthz`. A generated slug is 7 characters from `abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789`, drawn with `secrets.choice`. It is regenerated if it already exists or is reserved, with up to 5 attempts and then 500. Creating an existing slug returns 409.
15	- **R6 URL rules.** The scheme is `http` or `https` (case-insensitive). `urllib.parse.urlsplit(url).hostname` is non-empty. The URL is at most 2048 characters and contains no whitespace or control characters (code points < 0x21 or 0x7F). It is stored and redirected to verbatim.
16	- **R7 Resolve.** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with `Location: <url>` and an empty body. It atomically increments `clicks` and sets `last_clicked_at` to now.
17	- **R8 Missing and expired links.** An unknown slug returns 404. A link with `now >= expires_at` returns 410 and its click count is unchanged. Comparisons use whole seconds.
18	- **R9 List and inspect.** A token can list its own links (expired ones included) and fetch one link with its stats. Another token's link always returns 404, never 403.
19	- **R10 Delete.** A token can delete its own link. Afterwards the slug resolves 404 and is free to reuse.
20	- **R11 Rate limit.** Requests are counted per token in fixed 60-second windows aligned to the Unix epoch (`window_start = now - now % 60`). The limit is `--rate-limit` (default 60) counted requests per window. A request is counted when it reaches the rate-limit step (see precedence in Error handling), whatever its final status. Request number `limit + 1` and later in the same window return 429 with `Retry-After: <window_start + 60 - now>`. Counters are in memory and reset on restart. Redirects, `/healthz` and admin routes are not rate-limited.
21	- **R12 Clock.** "Now" is integer Unix seconds (floor of real time). With `--fake-clock <ISO>`, now is frozen at that instant and changes only through `POST /v1/admin/clock`. The fake clock is not persisted.
22	- **R13 Persistence.** Tokens, links, clicks and `last_clicked_at` survive a restart on the same `--db`.
23	- **R14 Concurrency.** The server is a `ThreadingHTTPServer`. N concurrent redirects to one slug leave `clicks == N` exactly.
24	- **R15 Shutdown.** On SIGINT, SIGTERM (POSIX) or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT/SIGBREAK (Windows), the server stops accepting connections, closes the DB and exits 0 within 5 seconds.
25	- **R16 Client.** CLI commands wrap the API. Each prints the response body to stdout, and uses the exit codes below.
26	
27	## Interface contract
28	
29	### Conventions
30	
31	- Timestamps are `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` in UTC with whole seconds. They are stored as INTEGER Unix seconds.
32	- JSON responses are encoded with `json.dumps(obj, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=True)` in UTF-8, with `Content-Type: application/json`. Every response sets `Content-Length`; a 204 response has an empty body and MUST send `Content-Length: 0`. Keys appear in exactly the order listed below.
33	- Request `Content-Type` is ignored. The body is read using `Content-Length` (absent means empty), and the maximum is 8192 bytes.
34	- Query strings are ignored on every route. Paths are matched exactly, with no trailing-slash normalisation. Any (method, path) pair not listed below returns 404 `not_found`.
35	- `short_url` is `http://127.0.0.1:<bound port>/<slug>`.
36	
37	**Link object** (key order is fixed): `{"slug", "url", "short_url", "created_at", "expires_at", "clicks", "last_clicked_at"}`. `expires_at` and `last_clicked_at` are `null` until they are set.
38	
39	### Server CLI
40	
41	```
42	python -m linkvault serve --db PATH --admin-key KEY [--port N] [--rate-limit N] [--fake-clock ISO]
43	```
44	
45	| Flag | Rule |
46	|---|---|
47	| `--db` | Required. The file is created if missing, and its parent directory must exist. |
48	| `--admin-key` | Required. Non-empty string. |
49	| `--port` | 0-65535, default 8000. The value 0 binds an OS-chosen free port. |
50	| `--rate-limit` | Integer >= 1, default 60. |
51	| `--fake-clock` | An ISO timestamp in the format above. It enables the admin clock route. |
52	
53	Ready line: `LISTENING http://127.0.0.1:<port>` followed by a line terminator, which may be `\n` or `\r\n`. It uses the actual bound port, is flushed immediately, and nothing else is written to stdout before it.
54	
55	Exit codes: 0 for a clean shutdown; 2 for a usage error (argparse); 3 if the port cannot be bound or the DB cannot be opened, with a message to stderr.
56	
57	### Endpoints
58	
59	| # | Method and path | Auth | Request body | Success response |
60	|---|---|---|---|---|
61	| E1 | `GET /healthz` | none | none | 200 `{"status":"ok"}` |
62	| E2 | `POST /v1/tokens` | `X-Admin-Key: <key>` | ignored | 201 `{"token":"lv_…","created_at":"…"}` |
63	| E3 | `POST /v1/links` | Bearer | `{"url": str, "slug"?: str, "expires_in"?: int}` | 201, link object |
64	| E4 | `GET /v1/links` | Bearer | none | 200 `{"links":[link…]}` ordered by `created_at` ascending, then `slug` ascending |
65	| E5 | `GET /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 200, link object |
66	| E6 | `DELETE /v1/links/<slug>` | Bearer | none | 204, empty body |
67	| E7 | `GET /<slug>` | none | none | 302, `Location: <url>`, `Content-Length: 0`, empty body |
68	| E8 | `POST /v1/admin/clock` | `X-Admin-Key` | `{"now": ISO}` | 200 `{"now":"…"}`. The route exists only with `--fake-clock`; otherwise it returns 404. Any valid timestamp is accepted. |
69	
70	E3 body rules:
71	- The body is a JSON object with no extra keys.
72	- `url` is required and must follow R6.
73	- `slug` is optional and must follow R5. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400).
74	- `expires_in` is optional. It is an integer from 1 to 31536000, and `bool` values are rejected. An explicit `null` is `invalid_request` (400). It sets `expires_at = created_at + expires_in`.
75	
76	E8 body rules:
77	- The body must be exactly `{"now": ISO}`, where ISO is a string in the timestamp format above.
78	- A missing `now` key, an extra key, a wrong type or an unparseable timestamp returns 400 `invalid_request`.
79	
80	A wrong or missing admin key on E2 or E8 returns 401. On E5, E6 and E7, a `<slug>` that fails `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{3,32}$` is a route mismatch, so it returns 404 at the route step, before auth.
81	
82	### DB schema (exact)
83	
84	```sql
85	PRAGMA user_version = 1;
86	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS tokens (
87	  token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
88	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL);
89	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS links (
90	  slug TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
91	  url TEXT NOT NULL,
92	  token_hash TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES tokens(token_hash),
93	  created_at INTEGER NOT NULL,
94	  expires_at INTEGER,
95	  clicks INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
96	  last_clicked_at INTEGER);
97	```
98	
99	A click is recorded with one statement: `UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1, last_clicked_at = ? WHERE slug = ?`.
100	
101	### Client CLI
102	
103	The server URL comes from `--server URL`, or else the `LINKVAULT_SERVER` environment variable. The token comes from `--token T`, or else `LINKVAULT_TOKEN`. Both options are accepted after the subcommand.
104	
105	| Command | Calls | Stdout on success |
106	|---|---|---|
107	| `token create --admin-key K` | E2 | Response JSON, one line |
108	| `shorten URL [--slug S] [--expires-in N]` | E3 | Response JSON, one line |
109	| `list` | E4 | Response JSON, one line |
110	| `stats SLUG` | E5 | Response JSON, one line |
111	| `delete SLUG` | E6 | Nothing |
112	
113	Output is re-serialised with the server's `json.dumps` settings and ends with `\n`. Client exit codes:
114	
115	| Code | Meaning | Output |
116	|---|---|---|
117	| 0 | 2xx response | as above |
118	| 1 | non-2xx response | Error JSON on stderr, stdout empty |
119	| 2 | usage error, or a missing server or token | Message on stderr |
120	| 3 | connection failure | Message on stderr |
121	
122	## Error handling
123	
124	Every error body has this shape: `{"error":{"code":"<code>","message":"<text>"}}`. Tests assert `code` only.
125	
126	| Condition | Status | code |
127	|---|---|---|
128	| No route matches the method and path; unknown or foreign slug | 404 | `not_found` |
129	| Missing, malformed or unknown bearer token; bad admin key | 401 | `unauthorized` |
130	| Over the rate limit (adds a `Retry-After` header) | 429 | `rate_limited` |
131	| `Content-Length` > 8192 (the response sets `Connection: close` and the body is not read) | 413 | `payload_too_large` |
132	| Body is not valid UTF-8 JSON, or is not an object | 400 | `invalid_json` |
133	| Schema violation: missing or extra key, wrong type, bad URL, slug, `expires_in` or `now` | 400 | `invalid_request` |
134	| Slug already exists, or is reserved (`healthz`) | 409 | `slug_taken` |
135	| Link expired (E7 only) | 410 | `gone` |
136	| Unhandled exception | 500 | `internal` |
137	
138	Precedence (first failure wins): route 404 → auth 401 → rate limit 429 → size 413 → JSON 400 → validation 400 → resource state 404/409/410.
139	
140	## Acceptance criteria
141	
142	- **AC1 (R1, R15):** `serve --port 0` prints exactly the `LISTENING` line. `GET /healthz` returns 200. SIGINT (or CTRL_BREAK_EVENT on Windows) makes it exit 0 within 5 s.
143	- **AC2 (R2):** E2 with the right key returns 201 and a token matching `^lv_[0-9a-f]{32}$`. With a wrong key it returns 401. The DB holds the SHA-256 of the token, never the plaintext.
144	- **AC3 (R3):** E3, E4 and E5 without a valid bearer token return 401 `unauthorized`.
145	- **AC4 (R4, R5):** E3 without `slug` returns a slug matching `^[a-z0-9]{7}$`. A custom `slug` is echoed back. A repeated slug returns 409. `healthz` and `ab` return 409 and 400 respectively.
146	- **AC5 (R6):** `ftp://x`, `javascript:alert(1)`, `http://`, a URL with a space, and a 2049-character URL each return 400 `invalid_request`.
147	- **AC6 (R7):** `GET /<slug>` returns 302 with the exact `Location`. A later E5 shows `clicks` 1 and `last_clicked_at` set to now.
148	- **AC7 (R8, R12):** With the fake clock at T and `expires_in=60`, the link resolves 302 at T+59 and 410 at T+60. Its clicks stay at the T+59 value.
149	- **AC8 (R9, R10):** Token B gets 404 on E5 and E6 for token A's slug. A's E4 lists only A's links in order. After E6, `GET /<slug>` returns 404 and the slug can be created again.
150	- **AC9 (R11):** With `--rate-limit 3` and the fake clock at a window start plus 10 s, requests 1-3 succeed. Request 4 returns 429 with `Retry-After: 50`. After the clock moves to the next window, the next request succeeds. Redirects are never limited.
151	- **AC10 (R13):** After a restart on the same DB, tokens still authenticate, and links and clicks are unchanged.
152	- **AC11 (R14):** 50 concurrent `GET /<slug>` requests leave `clicks == 50`.
153	- **AC12 (R16):** `shorten` prints the link JSON and exits 0. A 409 makes it exit 1 with empty stdout. An unreachable server makes it exit 3. A missing token makes it exit 2.

0	# AGENTS.md — geeky-orchestration
1	
2	Guidance for **any** AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Cursor, Windsurf,
3	Copilot CLI, Gemini CLI, or an SDK/LangGraph orchestrator) working with this
4	plugin's plan → execute → track workflow. Claude Code reads this via `@AGENTS.md`;
5	most other CLI agents read `AGENTS.md` natively.
6	
7	## Eval operator readiness
8	
9	This section applies only to operators in the source checkout. Contestant exports deliberately omit `evals/`; exported contestants must follow the canonical authorization and exported skills without looking for these operator files or adding a new approval gate. For source-checkout C0 preparation, read [current readiness](evals/c0-readiness.md) and [lessons learned](evals/lessons-learned.md). Generate fresh offline inventory and verify its exact HEAD, source hashes and prompt hash before a separately authorized live action. Local inventory and mock success grant no launch or telemetry publication authority. Preserve historical evidence and scores. Record desired and observed model/effort by role, the authorization reference, attempt/recovery limits, reserve and existing qualification waiver. Once a particular contestant run is authorized, retain the end-to-end workflow permissions already granted by its canonical prompt.
10	
11	## The workflow
12	
13	1. **spec-research** — research and write `feature-specification.md`.
14	2. **geeky-plan** — create the frozen planning package.
15	3. **plan-review** — validate alignment, coverage, sequencing, and readiness.
16	4. **geeky-status** — read-only status and resumption orientation at any packet stage.
17	5. **geeky-implement** — execute Ready tasks with validation and review gates.
18	6. **impl-review** — review delivered code through three domain-specific lanes.
19	7. **archive** — move completed planning artifacts into the archive structure.
20	
21	Use **geeky-orchestrator** when the requested entry point is unclear or when one
22	agent should administer the lifecycle. It examines repository evidence read-only
23	and recommends a workflow before mutation. Clear, explicit requests route to the
24	best matching skill after prerequisite checks. Material ambiguity is clarified;
25	stages are not auto-chained without end-to-end authorization.
26	
27	Full procedures live in the portable Skills under `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`.
28	
29	## Workflow terminology
30	
31	Use these meanings across skills, briefs and reports. They describe the orchestration
32	domain; retain the target project's own domain language. Existing filenames, schema
33	fields and checkpoint markers remain unchanged.
34	
35	| Term | Meaning |
36	|---|---|
37	| Planning package | Specification, plan, task contracts and tracking artifacts for one approved outcome. "Packet" is an alias; planning folder is its location. |
38	| Workflow stage | A lifecycle activity such as planning, implementation or final implementation review. Numbered "phases" inside a skill are procedure steps, not implementation phases. |
39	| Implementation phase | A group of tasks whose combined requirements are reviewed before advancement. "Wave" means a scheduling group unless the plan explicitly equates it with a phase. |
40	| Task | A bounded unit with an ID, scope, dependencies, acceptance criteria (ACs) and required validation. |
41	| Requirement / AC / Definition of Done | Required outcome or constraint / observable condition for satisfying it / completion conditions for the task. Required tests supply evidence; they do not replace ACs. |
42	| Task contract | The frozen task body and applicable approved requirements. A task brief conveys that contract to a worker. |
43	| Validation | Checks of the work. Validation evidence records what ran or was observed, against which inputs, and the result; a PASS claim alone is not evidence. |
44	| Review | Judgment of evidence against an assigned scope. Task review checks ACs/tests; phase review decides readiness to advance; final implementation review uses `impl-review`. Plan review evaluates the planning package. |
45	| Acceptance | The decision that required outcomes and gates for the stated scope are satisfied. Task Done, phase READY TO ADVANCE and final review PASS have different scopes; none grants release or deployment approval. |
46	| Finding | An evidenced discrepancy. A blocking finding prevents the current contract from being met; an optional improvement is a follow-up. Severity labels retain their review-stage meanings, not an automatic cross-stage mapping. |
47	| Execution batch / review batch | Tasks dispatched together / tasks sharing a reviewer assignment. Each phase has one review batch, the phase review: members wait in In Review until it clears, and each keeps its own verdict. |
48	| Orchestrator / worker / reviewer | Coordinates and accepts work / performs a bounded assignment / evaluates it. `geeky-coder` is the implementation worker; PM describes a planning or phase-review perspective. |
49	
50	## The planning-folder contract
51	
52	**Frozen** (never edit mid-run — they are the contract between plan and implement):
53	`implementation-plan.md`, `feature-specification.md`, `draft.md`, `references.md`,
54	and every `tasks/Tx-*.md` body. If the plan is genuinely wrong, surface it via the
55	kanban **Blocked** lane + `handoff.md` instead of editing the contract.
56	
57	**Mutable** (update continuously during implement):
58	`kanban.md` (single source of truth for lane status), `handoff.md` (running log),
59	and `tasks/Tx-*.notes.md` (per-task notes — these are writable, unlike the task bodies).
60	
61	Record a consequence for another task in that task's notes and in `handoff.md`.
62	
63	## Deterministic quality gates (run these — don't self-report)
64	
65	These replace "I updated the board / the task is done" with fail-stop checks.
66	Every gate: **arguments in, exit 0 = pass / exit 1 = fail, summary on stdout**,
67	optional `--json` / `-Json`. Each ships paired Python + PowerShell with identical
68	behavior. `geeky.manifest.json` is the machine-readable index of the same list.
69	
70	Paths below are relative to this plugin root (`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` in Claude Code).
71	Use `python3` where `python` is not on PATH; use `pwsh` (PowerShell 7+) for the `.ps1`.
72	
73	| Gate | When | Python | PowerShell |
74	|---|---|---|---|
75	| Planning-folder valid | start of implement/status | `python scripts/validate-planning-folder.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-planning-folder.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
76	| Task-file schema | end of plan; start of implement | `python scripts/validate-task-schema.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-task-schema.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
77	| Kanban integrity | after every lane move | `python scripts/validate-kanban.py --path "<folder>"` | `pwsh -File scripts/validate-kanban.ps1 -Path "<folder>"` |
78	| Definition of Done | in the Done step: move the task to Done, run this gate in the same step, move it back out on failure (D92) | `python scripts/check-dod.py --path "<folder>" --task <ID>` | `pwsh -File scripts/check-dod.ps1 -Path "<folder>" -Task <ID>` |
79	| Commit message | before each commit; pre-planning docs commits use `Tasks: none` | `python scripts/check-commit.py --message "<msg>"` (or `<FILE>`) | `pwsh -File scripts/check-commit.ps1 -Message "<msg>"` (or `<FILE>`) |
80	
81	**Feedback loop:** when a gate exits non-zero, read its output, fix the artifact,
82	and re-run the same gate until it exits 0 before proceeding.
83	
84	## How each agent type runs the gates
85	
86	- **Claude Code:** the frozen-artifact guard fires automatically via
87	  `hooks/hooks.json` (PreToolUse). Run the validators above as explicit steps.
88	- **Other CLI agents (Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Copilot, Gemini):** add an
89	  equivalent pre-edit/stop hook in your tool's config pointing at
90	  `hooks/guard-planning-contract.{py,ps1}` (it reads tool-call JSON on stdin,
91	  `--mode block` denies via JSON / exit 2). Invoke the validators as shell steps.
92	- **SDK / graph orchestrators (OpenAI Agents SDK, LangGraph):** call any validator
93	  with `subprocess.run([...])` inside a guardrail / node; raise a tripwire or
94	  `interrupt()` on a non-zero exit.
95	- **Any MCP-capable agent:** a bundled stdio MCP server (`geeky_mcp`, see `mcp/server.py`,
96	  registered in `.mcp.json`) exposes the gates as tools — `geeky_validate_planning_folder`,
97	  `geeky_validate_task_schema`, `geeky_validate_kanban`, `geeky_check_dod`,
98	  `geeky_check_commit`, `geeky_check_frozen_artifact` — for tool-style invocation with
99	  no per-framework hook config. Run it with `uv run --with "mcp>=1.2.0" python mcp/server.py`
100	  (or `pip install mcp && python mcp/server.py`).
101	
102	## Hard rules for implement
103	
104	Never push to a remote. Never `--no-verify`, `--force`, or `--amend`. Respect each
105	task's declared `Dependencies:`. Stop and finalize state (kanban + handoff) when a
106	task moves to Blocked. Verify task validation evidence against the tested revision,
107	commands and results; a coder's bare PASS claim is insufficient. Reuse valid evidence
108	and record the reason for any rerun. Task review checks ACs and defined tests; one reviewer dispatch at
109	phase end gives each task its verdict and the phase verdict. Phase
110	review checks collective requirements and must return READY TO ADVANCE before the
111	next phase starts; that verdict comes from a reviewer subagent whose agent ID is
112	recorded, and the last phase is included. Final implementation review uses `impl-review`.
113	The orchestrator never edits product code or tests; fixes go to `geeky-coder`. Batch independent
114	work and compatible fixes while preserving each task's verdict and resource isolation.
